docs.title: ABOUT THIS LAB
docs.text:
This portfolio documents practical exercises performed in a Microsoft Intune laboratory environment.

Each project includes its objectives, configuration, implementation details, validation results and technical evidence.

Focus areas: Microsoft Intune · Microsoft Entra ID · Windows 11 · Android Enterprise · Endpoint Security · Application Deployment

docs.title: Microsoft Intune Android Device Management
docs.text:
Explore Android Enterprise enrollment, device management and application protection capabilities through Microsoft Intune.

  • Android Enterprise

    Google's enterprise mobility framework.

  • Device Enrollment

    Corporate and personal device enrollment.

  • App Protection

    Protect organizational application data.

  • Work Profile

    Separate corporate and personal data.

Technical reference

docs.title: 1. Objectives
docs.text:
• Understand Android Enterprise architecture.
  • Explore Android enrollment methods.
  • Identify corporate and BYOD management scenarios.
  • Understand application protection policies.
  • Review device compliance and security.

docs.title: 2. Enrollment Models
docs.text: Enrollment type Description Fully Managed Corporate-owned device, fully managed Corporate-owned with Work Profile Corporate device with separated work and personal data Personally Owned Work Profile Personal device with a managed work profile Dedicated Device Corporate device for a specific organizational purpose

docs.title: 3. Management Architecture
docs.text:
• 01 · Android Device

    Corporate or personally owned device.

  • 02 · Enrollment

    Device enrolls through Android Enterprise.

  • 03 · Microsoft Intune

    Applies management and security policies.

  • 04 · Validation

    Review compliance and application status.

docs.title: 4. Application Management
docs.text:
• Managed Google Play integration.
  • Application assignments.
  • Managed application configuration.
  • Application protection policies.
  • Application deployment monitoring.

docs.title: 5. Security and Compliance
docs.text:
Important configuration areas:

  • Screen lock requirements.
  • Encryption requirements.
  • Minimum operating system version.
  • Device integrity.
  • Work profile protection.
  • Organizational data protection.

docs.title: 6. Validation
docs.text:
Validation should include:

  • Reviewing enrollment status.
  • Checking device compliance.
  • Verifying managed applications.
  • Reviewing policy deployment.
  • Investigating enrollment errors.

docs.title: 7. Implementation Considerations
docs.text:
• Select enrollment methods according to ownership.
  • Understand privacy boundaries in BYOD.
  • Apply appropriate application protection.
  • Test policies before broad deployment.
  • Communicate user enrollment requirements.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Android Enterprise supports multiple ownership models.
  • Work Profiles separate organizational and personal data.
  • Intune centralizes Android device management.
  • Application protection helps secure corporate information.

Explore endpoint administration automation, PowerShell scripting and Windows update management through Microsoft Intune.

Technical reference

docs.title: 1. Objectives
docs.text:
• Understand PowerShell integration with Intune.
  • Explore endpoint administration automation.
  • Understand Windows Update Rings.
  • Review update deployment and monitoring.
  • Identify common automation scenarios.

docs.title: 2. PowerShell and Intune
docs.text:
PowerShell can support endpoint administration and troubleshooting.

Typical use cases:

  • Collect device information.
  • Verify Windows configuration.
  • Troubleshoot application installations.
  • Inspect services and processes.
  • Automate repetitive administrative tasks.

docs.title: 3. Intune PowerShell Scripts
docs.text:
Scripts can be deployed to supported Windows devices through Intune.

Important configuration areas:

Setting Purpose Script content PowerShell commands Run as System or logged-on user Script signature Signature enforcement 64-bit PowerShell Execution architecture Assignment Target users or devices

docs.title: 4. Windows Update Rings
docs.text:
Update Rings help manage Windows quality and feature update behavior.

Configuration Purpose Quality updates Monthly security and reliability updates Feature updates Control Windows feature version Deadline settings Define installation deadlines Restart behavior Manage restart experience Deferral periods Delay update availability

docs.text:
• 01 · Configure

    Target the appropriate device groups.

  • 03 · Deploy

    Devices receive update policies.

  • 04 · Monitor

    Review update status and errors.

docs.title: 6. Monitoring and Troubleshooting
docs.text:

  • Reviewing update deployment reports.
  • Checking device update status.
  • Investigating installation errors.
  • Reviewing restart requirements.

docs.text:

  • Validate script results.

  • Plan update deadlines and restart behavior.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• PowerShell supports endpoint automation.
  • Intune provides centralized script deployment.

docs.title: Microsoft Intune Compliance Policies
docs.text:
Evaluate device health and security configuration to determine whether corporate endpoints meet organizational requirements.

  • Device Compliance

    Security and configuration evaluation.

  • Windows 11

    Managed endpoint platform.

  • Microsoft Intune

    Centralized compliance reporting.

  • Access Control

    Integration with Conditional Access.

Technical reference

docs.title: 1. Objectives
docs.text:
• Define device compliance requirements.
  • Evaluate Windows security settings.
  • Monitor device compliance status.
  • Understand the relationship between compliance and Conditional Access.

docs.title: 2. Architecture
docs.text:
• 01 · Windows Device

    Managed endpoint reports its configuration.

  • 02 · Intune Compliance Policy

    Evaluates configured compliance requirements.

  • 03 · Compliance Evaluation

    Device receives a compliance status.

  • 04 · Conditional Access

    Can use device compliance as an access condition.

docs.title: 3. Key Configuration Areas
docs.text: Configuration Purpose Minimum OS version Enforce supported Windows versions Firewall Require Windows Firewall Antivirus Require antivirus protection Antispyware Require antispyware protection Secure Boot Evaluate Secure Boot status BitLocker Require disk encryption

docs.title: 4. Compliance States
docs.text: Status Meaning Compliant Meets configured requirements Not compliant One or more requirements failed In grace period Remediation period is active Not evaluated Evaluation has not completed

docs.title: 5. Validation
docs.text:
Validation should include:

  • Reviewing the assigned compliance policy.
  • Checking device compliance status.
  • Reviewing individual setting results.
  • Investigating non-compliance reasons.
  • Confirming reporting in the Intune admin center.

docs.title: 6. Technical Considerations
docs.text:
• Compliance policies evaluate device requirements.
  • Configuration profiles apply device settings.
  • Conditional Access can restrict access based on compliance.
  • Compliance status depends on policy evaluation and device reporting.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Compliance policies help assess endpoint security posture.
  • Intune provides centralized compliance reporting.
  • Conditional Access can use compliance as an access condition.

docs.title: 4. Settings Catalog
docs.text:
The Settings Catalog provides a centralized interface to configure supported Windows settings.

Typical use cases:

  • Configure Windows experience.
  • Manage privacy settings.
  • Configure Microsoft Edge.
  • Apply security configurations.
  • Control operating system behavior.

docs.title: 5. Assignment and Deployment
docs.text:
Configuration profiles can be assigned to:

  • Device groups

Important considerations:

  • Assignment scope
  • Included and excluded groups
  • Assignment filters
  • Policy conflicts

docs.title: 6. Validation
docs.text:
Validation should include:

  • Reviewing profile deployment status.
  • Checking device-level configuration results.
  • Identifying configuration errors.
  • Reviewing policy conflicts.
  • Confirming settings on the endpoint.

docs.title: 7. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Common investigation areas:

  • Device synchronization
  • Unsupported settings
  • Conflicting policies
  • Assignment scope
  • Windows edition compatibility
  • Configuration reporting delays

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Configuration profiles centralize endpoint settings.
  • Settings Catalog provides granular configuration options.
  • Assignments determine which devices receive policies.
  • Deployment monitoring is essential for troubleshooting.

docs.title: Microsoft Intune Endpoint Protection
docs.text:
Explore Windows endpoint security capabilities managed through Microsoft Intune, including practical implementations and technical security concepts.

  • Microsoft Defender Antivirus

    Antivirus configuration and threat protection.

  • Windows Account Protection

    Credential Guard and Windows Hello for Business.

  • Windows Security Baselines

    Recommended Windows security configurations.

  • Additional Security Controls

    BitLocker, Windows Firewall and Attack Surface Reduction concepts.

Practical projects available

docs.title: 1. Objectives
docs.text:
• Understand endpoint security policy management.
  • Configure Windows security controls through Microsoft Intune.
  • Explore Microsoft Defender Antivirus capabilities.
  • Understand credential protection and Windows security baselines.
  • Monitor policy deployment and device status.

docs.title: 2. Security Architecture
docs.text:
Microsoft Intune acts as the central management platform for endpoint security policies.

Security configurations are assigned to Windows devices through policy profiles and security baselines.

The architecture includes:

  • Microsoft Intune: Centralized policy management.
  • Windows Security Policies: Security configuration and enforcement.
  • Windows Devices: Receive and apply assigned configurations.
  • Monitoring: Deployment status and configuration validation.

docs.title: 3. Implemented Security Components
docs.text:
The following security capabilities have been configured and documented in the lab environment.

Component Lab Status Microsoft Defender Antivirus Implemented Windows Security Baseline Implemented Windows Account Protection Implemented

docs.title: 4. Microsoft Defender Antivirus
docs.text:
Microsoft Defender Antivirus provides built-in Windows malware and threat protection.

Key configuration areas explored in the lab:

  • Real-time protection.
  • Cloud-delivered protection.
  • Behavior monitoring.
  • Archive and email scanning.
  • Script scanning.
  • Network Protection.
  • Potentially unwanted application protection.

docs.title: 5. Windows Account Protection
docs.text:
Account Protection policies help strengthen endpoint credential security.

Configuration areas implemented:

  • Microsoft Defender Credential Guard.
  • Credential Guard with UEFI Lock.
  • Windows Hello for Business.
  • Minimum PIN length requirements.

docs.title: 6. Windows Security Baselines
docs.text:
Security baselines provide recommended security configurations for Windows devices.

The lab includes a Windows Security Baseline deployment through Microsoft Intune.

Key security areas include:

  • Microsoft Defender settings.
  • User Account Control.
  • BitLocker-related security settings.
  • Windows Firewall.
  • Remote Desktop security.
  • SmartScreen and other Windows protections.

docs.title: 7. Additional Endpoint Security Concepts
docs.text:
The following technologies are relevant to endpoint security management and remain areas for further practical exploration:

Component Purpose BitLocker Protect data through disk encryption. Windows Firewall Control network traffic. Attack Surface Reduction Reduce exposure to common attack techniques.

These components are included as technical reference topics and are not presented as separately implemented lab projects.

docs.title: 8. Deployment and Validation
docs.text:
Endpoint security policy validation includes:

  • Reviewing assigned security policies.
  • Checking device deployment status.
  • Monitoring successful and failed assignments.
  • Reviewing policy conflicts.
  • Verifying configured security settings where applicable.

docs.title: 9. Implementation Considerations
docs.text:
• Test policies with a pilot device group.
  • Review existing Windows security configurations.
  • Consider compatibility before enforcing settings.
  • Monitor policy conflicts and deployment errors.
  • Protect sensitive recovery information.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Microsoft Intune centralizes endpoint security policy management.
  • Defender Antivirus provides essential malware protection.
  • Account Protection strengthens credential security.
  • Security Baselines help standardize Windows security configurations.
  • Deployment monitoring is essential for validating endpoint security policies.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
This lab demonstrates the creation of a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy designed to evaluate access based on device compliance.

The policy remains in Report-only mode, allowing its potential impact to be evaluated without enforcing access restrictions.

docs.title: Policy Configuration
docs.text: Setting Configuration Policy name Must be compliant Users All users Excluded users None Target resources No resources selected Grant control Require device to be marked as compliant Device platforms Any device, with 4 exclusions Network Not configured Client apps 1 included Policy state Report-only

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:
The configured grant control requires devices to be marked as compliant.

In Report-only mode, Microsoft Entra evaluates policy conditions during sign-in without enforcing the access control requirement.

docs.title: Validation and Current Status
docs.text:
The policy configuration confirms:

  • Report-only mode is enabled.
  • All users are included, with no exclusions.
  • The compliant-device grant control is selected.
  • No target resources are currently selected.

Current status: Initial lab configuration. The policy is not fully scoped because no target resources have been selected.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text: This project demonstrates the configuration and monitoring of a Windows Update Ring policy using Microsoft Intune on a Windows 11 Enterprise virtual machine.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Component Configuration Platform Windows 11 Enterprise Management Microsoft Intune Device Windows 11 Virtual Machine Policy type Windows Update Ring Assignment Windows devices

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The Windows Update Ring policy was configured in Microsoft Intune to manage Windows update behavior, including update installation and management settings.

docs.title: Deployment and Validation
docs.text:
The policy was assigned to the Windows devices group.

Microsoft Intune reported the policy status as Running for the target device, WINDOWS11.

During validation, Windows Update on the virtual machine reported that the device was up to date. An additional update download was also observed.

The Intune status is documented as reported and is not presented as a completed deployment.
